entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10577"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 47</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Jer.47.1-Jer.47.7">Jr 47:1-7</reference>. Prophecy against the Philistines.</title> <div sID="gen18886" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10577"/>1. Pharaoh-necho probably smote Gaza on his return after defeating Josiah at Megiddo (<reference osisRef="2Chr.35.20">2Ch 35:20</reference>) [Grotius]. Or, Pharaoh-hophra (<reference osisRef="Jer.37.5">Jr 37:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.37.7">7</reference>) is intended: probably on his return from his fruitless attempt to save Jerusalem from the Chaldeans, he smote Gaza in order that his expedition might not be thought altogether in vain [Calvin] (<reference osisRef="Amos.1.6">Am 1:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.1.7">7</reference>). <div eID="gen18886" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 47 Jr 47:1-7 . Prophecy against the Philistines. 1. Pharaoh-necho probably smote Gaza on his return after defeating Josiah at Megiddo ( 2Ch 35:20 ) [Grotius]. Or, Pharaoh-hophra ( Jr 37:5 , 7 ) is intended: probably on his return from his fruitless attempt to save Jerusalem from the Chaldeans, he smote Gaza in order that his expedition might not be thought altogether in vain [Calvin] ( Am 1:6 , 7 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10578"/><div sID="gen18887" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10578"/><hi type="bold">2. waters--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.8.7">Is 8:7</reference>). The Chaldeans from the north are compared to the overwhelming waters of their own Euphrates. The smiting of Gaza was to be only the prelude of a greater disaster to the Philistines. Nebuzara-dan was left by Nebuchadnezzar, after he had taken Jerusalem, to subdue the rest of the adjoining cities and country. <div eID="gen18887" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10580"/><div sID="gen18891" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10580"/><hi type="bold">4. every helper--</hi>The Philistines, being neighbors to the Phoenicians of Tyre and Sidon, would naturally make common cause with them in the case of invasion. These cities would have no helper left when the Philistines should be destroyed.<div eID="gen18891" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18892" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Caphtor--</hi>the Caphtorim and Philistines both came from Mizraim (<reference osisRef="Gen.10.13">Ge 10:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="Gen.10.14">14</reference>). The Philistines are said to have been delivered by God from Caphtor (<reference osisRef="Amos.9.7">Am 9:7</reference>). Perhaps before the time of Moses they dwelt near and were subjugated by the Caphtorim (<reference osisRef="Deut.2.23">De 2:23</reference>) and subsequently delivered. "The remnant" means here those still left after the Egyptians had attacked Gaza and Palestine; or rather, those left of the Caphtorim after the Chaldeans had attacked them previous to their attack on the Philistines. Some identify Caphtor with Cappadocia; Gesenius, with Crete (<reference osisRef="Ezek.25.16">Eze 25:16</reference>, Cherethims); Kitto, Cyprus. Between Palestine and Idumea there was a city Caparorsa; and their close connection with Palestine on the one hand, and Egypt (Mizraim, <reference osisRef="Gen.10.13">Ge 10:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="Gen.10.14">14</reference>) on the other hand, makes this locality the most likely. <div eID="gen18892" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10581"/><div sID="gen18893" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10581"/><hi type="bold">5. Baldness ... cut thyself--</hi>Palestine is represented as a female who has torn off her hair and cut her flesh, the heathenish (<reference osisRef="Lev.19.28">Le 19:28</reference>) token of mourning (<reference osisRef="Jer.48.37">Jr 48:37</reference>).<div eID="gen18893" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18894" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">their valley--</hi>the long strip of low plain occupied by the Philistines along the Mediterranean, west of the mountains of Judea. The Septuagint reads Anakim, the remains of whom were settled in those regions (<reference osisRef="Num.13.28">Nu 13:28</reference>). Joshua dislodged them so that none were left but in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod (<reference osisRef="Josh.11.21">Jos 11:21</reference>, <reference osisRef="Josh.11.22">22</reference>). But the parallel (<reference osisRef="Jer.47.7">Jr 47:7</reference>), "Ashkelon ... the sea-shore," established English Version here, "Ashkelon ... their valley." <div eID="gen18894" type="x-p"/>
